title: Harness-Portable Orchestrator Prompt Contract
non_product_work: Create a bounded role-scoped workflow orchestration follow-on that defines a repo-native, harness-portable Work Item PM orchestrator prompt contract and validation path without making the prompt canonical workflow authority or implementing runtime role/execution packets.
origin: Current repo context records no active work item after BANDIT-064 closeout and directs Repo PM to triage the remaining BANDIT-GAP-ROLE-SCOPED-WORKFLOW-ORCHESTRATION source-material gap into a bounded work item or explicit disposition before unrelated cockpit product work. docs/design/role-scoped-workflow-orchestration.md and the BANDIT-057/BANDIT-058 retrospectives identify Execution And Role Input Packets as the next role-scoped source-material idea, but docs/decisions/2026-06-05-harness-agnostic-cli-trust-layer.md supersedes Pi/Aperture runtime work and says an orchestrator prompt may guide a harness while Bandit CLI remains the trust authority. This chore scopes only that harness-portable prompt contract boundary.
scope: Define a repo-native Work Item PM orchestrator prompt contract for formation-approved work items that any harness or Process Adapter may use as guidance for a coherent Stage 2 through Stage 6 session.

Keep the orchestrator prompt explicitly non-authoritative: it may instruct a runtime how to call Bandit CLI commands and how to preserve stage evidence, but it cannot replace the brief, coordination log, Work Item PM plan artifact, RED evidence, implementation evidence, review evidence, landing evidence, retrospective evidence, bootstrap-gap ledger, current context, roadmap, or Trust Verifier verdicts.

Require the prompt contract to preserve Repo PM, Work Item PM, Test Writer, Implementation Writer, Reviewer, Landing Agent, and Closeout Agent authority boundaries, including the Permanent Test Ownership Boundary and Bootstrap Model-Family Separation.

Require the prompt contract to anchor execution in current repo-derived context: the approved brief, `formation_approved` coordination evidence, `orchestration_plan_recorded` evidence when required, stage capability scope, token-cost failsafe boundaries, current bootstrap-gap state, and current operator-input status.

Require the prompt contract to direct every stage transition through existing or explicitly scoped Bandit evidence and validation commands rather than chat memory, live provider state, queue state, model memory, or harness-local status.

Add a local policy/template/validator surface, expected as `.bandit/policy/orchestrator-prompts.json`, `docs/templates/work-item-pm-orchestrator-prompt.md`, `src/state/orchestrator-prompts.ts`, `src/commands/orchestrator-prompts.ts`, and `test/orchestrator-prompts.test.mjs`, only as needed to enforce the prompt contract.

Make validation fail closed when an orchestrator prompt grants itself canonical workflow authority, skips formation or plan-mode gates, gives Work Item PM authority to write tests or implementation, lets Stage 3 edit tests, treats same-model RED and implementation as acceptable during bootstrap, bypasses reviewer or landing gates, mutates repo workflow state outside CLI commands, or depends on live network/provider state as trust evidence.

Preserve the harness-agnostic CLI Trust Layer boundary: the prompt is an adapter-facing guidance artifact; Bandit remains the deterministic CLI trust layer and existing gate commands remain authoritative until a separately approved Trust Verifier cutover exists.
Record CLEAN_CODE.md read evidence in Stage 1; CLEAN_CODE.md was read on 2026-06-07 before creating this spec, and clean-code compliance must be evaluated before landing.

Stage sequence expectation: Repo PM creates this Stage 1 brief, formation review is required before approval, Work Item PM may start only after `formation_approved`, Work Item PM plan-mode evidence remains required before Stage 2 where applicable, Stage 2 RED evidence must precede implementation, Stage 3 implementation must preserve test ownership, Stage 4 must run CodeRabbit and Local Qwen or record honest provider-refusal evidence, Stage 5 must record landing verdict/action evidence, and Stage 6 must record retrospective and gap disposition before any later work starts.

Stage capability scope for this chore: Codex PM/Repo PM owns Stage 1 brief creation, formation routing, and context-artifact synchronization; Test Writer owns Stage 2 RED evidence; if Codex authors or materially edits Stage 2 RED tests, Stage 3 implementation is assigned to Claude through the bootstrap Process Adapter path; Stage 3 Implementation Writer has no authority to edit tests, test helpers, fixtures, RED evidence, acceptance mappings, formation evidence, review evidence, landing evidence, or retrospective evidence; reviewers own Stage 4 evidence; Landing Agent owns Stage 5 verdict/action evidence; Closeout Agent/Codex PM owns Stage 6 closeout evidence.

Token-cost failsafe boundary: use existing Token-Cost Failsafe policy for abnormal-run guardrails if paid, high-token, reviewer, or long-running execution becomes necessary; this chore must not approve new provider-pricing evidence, spend-class approval, paid reviewer promotion, recurring paid routing, or operator-owned cost/risk overrides.

Future-work scope: this chore must not implement generated execution packets, generated role input packets, live agent-to-agent channels, True Agent lifecycle, Pi/Aperture agent-scope schema or projection work, work queues, scheduler execution, claim authority, worktree lifecycle execution, diff-based write validation, same-agent repair continuation, landing/closeout handoff automation, Trust Verifier cutover, old gate replacement or wrapping, live evidence capture helpers, reviewer/test execution inside trust verification, cockpit product work, dependency or lockfile changes, external service setup, merge/push/deploy behavior, product UAT scope, installed global skill edits, or broader product/policy changes.
acceptance_criteria: The chore brief exists at `docs/work/<ID>/brief.md` and links to `BANDIT-GAP-ROLE-SCOPED-WORKFLOW-ORCHESTRATION` as the active bootstrap gap while making clear this is a bounded orchestrator-prompt contract slice, not full role-scoped runtime implementation.

Stage 1 brief evidence records `CLEAN_CODE.md` read evidence, source authority, scope and out-of-scope, stage capability scope, operator-input status, model-family separation, Permanent Test Ownership Boundary, required evidence, expected files, stage sequence, and forbidden actions.

Focused RED evidence proves the repo currently lacks a repo-native Work Item PM orchestrator prompt contract and validation path that preserve Bandit CLI authority while allowing harness-portable orchestration guidance.

A local prompt contract or policy artifact defines required prompt sections for current repo state, stage sequence, required evidence, role boundaries, validation commands, known blockers, stop conditions, forbidden actions, and CLI authority.

The contract requires prompts to consume only repo-derived local evidence as trust inputs and to treat live harness state, provider dashboards, model memory, queue state, and chat text as non-authoritative unless first materialized as local evidence.

Validation fails closed for prompts that skip Formation Gate evidence, skip Work Item PM plan-mode evidence when required, bypass RED-before-implementation sequencing, erode Test Writer or Implementation Writer ownership, allow Stage 3 test edits, allow same-model RED and implementation during bootstrap, bypass reviewer or landing gates, mutate workflow state outside CLI commands, or claim Trust Verifier cutover authority.

The orchestrator prompt contract remains adapter guidance and cannot replace canonical brief, coordination, work-item plan, RED, implementation, review, landing, retrospective, roadmap, current-context, bootstrap-gap, or trust-verifier authority.

The implementation preserves existing `work-item-pm start`, role contract, role-run manifest, coordination-log, stage-capability-scope, token-cost-failsafe, risk-classification, supply-chain-gate, input-quarantine, operator-boundary, and Trust Verifier Compatibility Period behavior unless a focused acceptance criterion requires a narrow validation integration.

The implementation preserves Permanent Test Ownership Boundary and Bootstrap Model-Family Separation: if Codex authors or materially edits Stage 2 RED tests, Stage 3 implementation goes to Claude, and the Stage 3 Writer cannot edit tests, test helpers, fixtures, RED evidence, or acceptance mappings for this work item.
Stage 4 review evidence uses pre-PR CodeRabbit and Local Qwen at the current review-subject hash unless honest provider refusal or bootstrap-gap evidence is recorded.
Layered risk-classification and supply-chain gate evidence are recorded before landing because this chore touches local prompt/template/policy surfaces that guide future agent execution.
Clean-code compliance is evaluated before landing; any accepted non-blocking concern becomes a tagged follow-up or explicit no-action decision.

`BANDIT-GAP-ROLE-SCOPED-WORKFLOW-ORCHESTRATION` is not fully resolved by this chore unless Stage 6 closeout explicitly proves no remaining source-material work is queued or records an explicit no-action/deferred disposition for the rest of the umbrella.
